result:
Implemented and committed both pieces of the brief: **`src/validate.js`** — `validate({ email, password })` returns per-field messages: missing/blank email → "Enter your email address", email without `@` → "Enter a valid email address", missing password → "Enter a password", password under 8 chars → "Use at least 8 characters". Valid input returns `{}`. **`src/form.js`** — `render({ values, errors, submitting })`: - Labeled `email`/`password` inputs with matching `id`/`name`, values HTML-escaped (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`) - Errored fields get `aria-invalid="true"`, `aria-describedby="-error"`, and a `

` right after the input; clean fields get neither - An `

` summary with a `
    ` of messages linking to each field (``) appears before the fields only when errors exist - `submitting: true` adds `aria-busy="true"` to the form and disables the button with "Signing up…" text; otherwise it reads "Sign up" **Verification:** wrote `test/validate.test.js` (8 cases covering every validation rule and combinations) and expanded `test/form.test.js` (10 cases covering labels/ids, escaping, error attributes/summary presence and absence, ordering, and the submitting state). Ran `npm test` — all 18 tests pass. Work is committed as `d52b0a1`.
